definitions.note: 28 across is a word for an item of clothing, so the plural stands for the plural

indicators.note: to interrupt is to break into the middle of something, so one word sits inside the other

parts.note: clots are fools, idiots
he is the pronoun for a man

explanation.surface: A man barges in on a pair of idiots dressed in their best outfits.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition '28s' points to the answer to 28 across, GARMENT, made plural.
explanation.definitionFit: Garments are articles of dress, and the collective plural for them all is a straightforward synonym.

parts.note: looks like an art remark about J. M. W. Turner, but describes a revolving drum that is turned to haul in a rope, a painter being a boat's mooring line

explanation.surface: A comment on the artist Turner and his sketching.
explanation.definitionFit: A capstan is a rotating drum turned to wind in cables, such as a boat's painter rope.

clue.text: Very large plant absorbs one in gradual assimilation

parts.note: OS is the clothing size abbreviation for outsize

indicators.note: absorbs means one word takes the other inside it

parts.note: moss is a small plant
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A huge plant soaks up a single item as part of slow absorption.
explanation.definitionFit: Osmosis is used figuratively for gradually absorbing ideas or knowledge without effort.

indicators.note: contains says the run of letters is held within the words beside it

explanation.surface: A claim that lichen holds a natural colouring.
explanation.definitionFit: Henna is a reddish dye made from the leaves of a shrub, used on hair and skin.

clue.text: Recently built a cracking shop for ceramics

indicators.note: cracking means breaking into the word for shop, so the other pieces sit inside it

parts.note: a store is a shop
something recently built is new

explanation.surface: A newly opened pottery shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cracking' hints at broken pottery but tells NEW and A to break into STORE.
explanation.definitionFit: Stoneware is a dense, hard type of pottery, one class of ceramics.

parts.note: slacks look like a verb meaning idles, but read as a noun they are informal trousers, the sort of relaxed clothes worn off duty

explanation.surface: A one-word query about loafing at work, or about trousers.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal clothes, slacks among them, are called by this word, so trousers stand as an example.

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
A, D and E are notes of the scale, and T stands for te in tonic sol-fa

explanation.surface: A student is spotted writing things down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking' only joins the two pieces; T is te as written in tonic sol-fa shorthand.
explanation.definitionFit: A cadet is a young person training for the armed forces or police.

clue.text: Incredibly small club in Finish cape

indicators.note: in puts the word for club inside the Finnish name

parts.note: read as Finnish: Suomi is the Finns' own name for their country
a bat is a club used in sport
C is the map abbreviation for cape

explanation.surface: A tiny club found in a Finnish headland.
explanation.definitionFit: Subatomic describes particles smaller than an atom, so it is used for something unbelievably tiny.

definitions.meaning: a relation is a narrative, a report of events
of no worth or significance is said to be of no consequence

explanation.definitionFit: An account is a narrative report, and something of account has significance.

indicators.note: in places the officer inside the word for fine

parts.note: sheer fabric is fine and thin
LT is the abbreviation for lieutenant, an officer

explanation.surface: An officer is in fine cover, well hidden.
explanation.definitionFit: A shelter is a place giving protection, which is cover.

parts.note: pi is schoolboy slang for pious, holy
men are people
taken as written

explanation.surface: Devout folk adopt a seasoning for their meals.
explanation.walkthrough: PI, short for pious, is a crossword favourite for 'holy'; 'taking' is only a joining word.
explanation.definitionFit: Pimento is allspice, the dried berry used as a seasoning, so it is one kind of spice.

clue.text: Bleached badly without hot water flowing through

indicators.note: badly signals that the letters are put together wrongly, rearranged
without asks for a letter to be left out of the word beside it

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: Something was bleached poorly because no hot water ran through the machine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without hot' drops H from BLEACHED, leaving BLEACED, which 'badly' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A debacle originally meant a violent rush of water, as when river ice breaks up and floods through.

clue.text: Note plant's part in dry statement

indicators.note: in places the first pieces inside the word for dry

parts.note: TT, teetotal, means dry or abstaining from drink
E is a musical note
the stamen is the pollen-bearing part of a flower

explanation.surface: A musical note and a flower's anatomy appear within a dull declaration.
explanation.definitionFit: A testament is a solemn declaration or attestation of something, such as a will or creed.

parts.note: to rust is to decay or decline through neglect

explanation.surface: Losing religion over the years.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a joining word between the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Trust is confident belief or reliance, which is a sense of faith.

clue.text: Sound heard in "as thin as a lath"

indicators.note: a sound heard in a phrase is caught sitting within its words, so the letters run across them

explanation.surface: A voice so pinched it could be described as thin as a lath.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks make the phrase look like the sound, but the run spans thiN AS A Lath.
explanation.definitionFit: A nasal is a speech sound produced through the nose, such as M or N.

clue.text: Two boys in green like snow

definitions.meaning: an allusion to the folk song Green Grow the Rushes, O

explanation.definitionFit: Lily-white means pure white, as snow is, and names the song's pair of boys.

indicators.note: the clue word that signals this step

parts.note: read as change plus over: alter means change, and over says it goes around the next word
taken as written

explanation.surface: A switch of times happening on the flight deck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Changeover' reads as one noun but must be split into two words, the second telling the first to go around 'time'; the definition is cryptic, naming where the instrument sits.
explanation.definitionFit: An altimeter is a height-measuring instrument found among the controls in an aircraft cockpit.

clue.text: Object about stream producing a shiver

indicators.note: about means the word for object goes around the other

parts.note: a thing is an object
a rill is a small stream

explanation.surface: An object near a stream gives someone the shivers.
explanation.definitionFit: Something thrilling excites a person so much it sends a tingle or shudder through them.

definitions.meaning: a trifle is a thing of little importance
read literally, a weak or minor ale is what is served in a pub bar

explanation.surface: A dessert served in the pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Small beer means a trivial matter, and literally it is weak beer you might drink at a bar.

clue.text: Upsets first cause problem, then doubt

indicators.note: problem is read as a word for trouble, so the letters are thrown into disorder
first takes the opening letter of the word cause

explanation.surface: Disruptions first create a difficulty and then uncertainty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'then' is a joining word; the definition is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To suspect is to doubt someone's honesty or a claim's truth.

indicators.note: heard means the words are said out loud and spelt as another word

parts.note: a shower is rain, so this reads as a rain

explanation.surface: A downpour heard calling out to one's bank account.
explanation.walkthrough: 7 down is ACCOUNT, so 'call of 7' is a call to account.
explanation.definitionFit: To arraign is to call someone before a court to answer, which is calling them to account.

clue.text: Cringe if hundred and one in the red

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
someone in the red owes money, so is an ower

explanation.surface: You would shrink if you were a hundred and one and in debt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'if' and 'and' are joining words; 'one in the red' is one who owes.
explanation.definitionFit: To cower is to crouch or shrink back in fear, which is to cringe.

clue.text: Get to grips rather than come to blows

definitions.text: Get to grips rather than come to blows

parts.words: Get to grips rather than come to blows
parts.note: a combat sport where fighters grapple holds instead of punching

explanation.surface: Advice to tackle an issue instead of fighting about it.
explanation.definitionFit: Wrestling is grappling an opponent with holds, as opposed to striking punches as in boxing.

indicators.note: circulating means going round, so the letters are turned backwards
from says the letters are taken out of the words beside it

explanation.surface: Pulling the gangster film Get Carter from distribution.
explanation.walkthrough: Get Carter is a 1971 British gangster film. Reading geT CARTER backwards gives the run.
explanation.definitionFit: To retract is to withdraw a statement or draw something back in.

clue.text: Withered stems have growth returning to a point

parts.note: S, south, is one of the points of the compass

indicators.note: returning means the word for growth goes back the other way

parts.note: a wart is a small growth on the skin

explanation.surface: Dried-out stalks show new shoots coming back to a tip.
explanation.definitionFit: Straw is the dried stalks of cereal plants left after threshing.

clue.text: Flier is most experienced when taking credit after good start

indicators.note: after puts the longer piece behind the opening letter
the start of the word good is its opening letter
taking means the word for most experienced takes in the abbreviation

parts.note: the oldest have the most experience

explanation.surface: An aviator, the most seasoned, gets recognition after a good beginning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flier' suggests a pilot, but it is a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The goldcrest is a tiny European songbird, so it is a flier in the sense of a flying creature.

definitions.meaning: a cat-like mammal of the civet family
Jean ... was a French novelist and playwright

explanation.definitionFit: The genet is a civet-family mammal, and Genet is a French writer of note.

indicators.note: in a down clue over puts the first piece above the next

parts.note: Lear is Shakespeare's tragic king

explanation.surface: A Catholic king is passed over for the throne.
explanation.definitionFit: To clear an obstacle is to pass over it without touching, as a jumper clears a bar.

parts.note: a print run sends out one batch of a book, and the first time round makes the famous collector's version

explanation.surface: A book's first print run going out.
explanation.definitionFit: An edition is all the copies of a book printed in one run, the first being prized.

parts.note: sounds like a proverb about fame, but in physics every body has a moment of resistance to turning

explanation.surface: A proverb that everyone gets their fifteen minutes.
explanation.definitionFit: In physics every massive body has a moment of inertia, its resistance to changes in rotation.

clue.text: Browning's man that's refined touching line

parts.note: a tan is a browning of the skin; the poet Browning is the surface decoy
a gent is a gentleman, a refined man

explanation.surface: The poet Robert Browning's cultivated hero is meant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Browning' looks like the poet, but it is tanning in the sun.
explanation.definitionFit: In geometry a tangent is a straight line touching a curve at one point.

clue.text: It's worn out great men heartlessly

indicators.note: out signals the letters are put out of order, rearranged
heartlessly removes the central letter of the word men

explanation.surface: Fame fades: great men are spent and treated without compassion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartlessly' cuts MEN to MN; 'out' rearranges GREAT plus MN.
explanation.definitionFit: A garment is an item of clothing, something worn.
